mechanism: When banks tighten C&I lending standards, firms lose access to credit, investment and hiring slow, and default risk rises; tightening historically builds before and during recessions, so the credit-crunch prior is to reduce equity exposure when net tightening is high or rising.
key_finding: As known at the time (real-time DRTSCILM vintages from 2010-04-20), the rule selected on in-sample data uses chg_4q (procyclical) at L3q with OOS Sharpe 0.81 versus buy-and-hold 0.91.
caveats: Quarterly survey with a small OOS window; the winner is search-selected and needs a frozen-rule holdout.
The real-time (as known at the time) archive starts in 2010, so the training period is short and holds no recession.
The data is DRTSCILM (large and middle-market firms), not the small-firm series DRTSCIS the pair id names.
narrative_summary: Bank C&I lending standards (SLOOS) are tested as a credit-cycle overlay for SPY.

known_stress_episodes.note: Net tightening reached its survey highs.
